title: Maximum Increasing Triplet Value
summary: For an array nums, find the highest value of a triplet (i, j, k) where i < j < k and nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k].
statement: For an array nums, find the highest value of a triplet (i, j, k) where i < j < k and nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k]. The value of the triplet is calculated as nums[i] - nums[j] + nums[k].
constraints: nums contains at least three positive integers.
Choose indices i<j<k with strictly increasing values nums[i]<nums[j]<nums[k].
Maximize nums[i]-nums[j]+nums[k], returning zero when no valid triplet exists.
hints: For each middle index, the best endpoints are the largest earlier value below it and the largest later value above it.
Precompute suffix maxima and use a compressed Fenwick maximum tree to query earlier values by rank.
At j, query ranks below nums[j]; if suffix[j+1]>nums[j], maximize left-nums[j]+suffix[j+1]; then insert nums[j].
The strict rank query and suffix condition enumerate exactly valid middles, while choosing the largest endpoints maximizes the expression for that middle.
editorial: The strict rank query and suffix condition enumerate exactly valid middles, while choosing the largest endpoints maximizes the expression for that middle.

tests.explanation: The only triplet is increasing and has value five minus six plus nine, which is eight.
Indices zero, two, and four form 1<3<19 with value seventeen, the maximum.
